cap_window_confirmation: Offsets 4/5/4/1 resolved to 38/39/38/35 against a level-36 party: cap 36 on Medium, matching the dossier seed line. These are the highest individual levels in my block - Pupitar at cap+3 is the single highest-levelled opponent I played.
party_pool_audit: Block core led by Weavile + Gyarados, the two Ice carriers. All six gate <= 36 with source maps passed before Route 113.
pre_declared_strategy_checks: Gabite attacks while Pupitar uses Helping Hand or its own attack
Shelgon's Dragon Dance and Turtonator's Shell Smash are alternate development paths, and successive setup users are not exposed unnecessarily
Turtonator's White Herb repairs the Shell Smash defense drops once and is actually consumed
The three unevolved members' Eviolite bulk is real
Gabite has no Ground STAB; Pupitar supplies the Ground offense
Every opposing Protect has a payoff

attempts.narrative: T1 Wyatt switched Gabite out for Turtonator, which was sensible - Gabite is 4x weak to the Ice I had just shown him - but Pupitar had simultaneously selected Helping Hand on that same partner, and it failed outright. My Knock Off retargeted onto the incoming Turtonator and removed its White Herb, and a Mold Breaker Ice Fang took it to 6. T2 Ice Shard finished Turtonator before it could Shell Smash; Pupitar Protected and blocked a 4x Waterfall. T3 Pupitar's Helping Hand landed this time but Shelgon died to Triple Axel before it could use the boost, and Waterfall - 4x into Rock/Ground - killed a 140 HP Eviolite Pupitar in one hit. T4 Gabite came back and Ice Shard, 4x into Dragon/Ground, killed it. Four turns, zero player faints, and my Mega Gyarados finished on 125 of 125 without taking a single point of damage.

strategy_checks.check: Gabite attacks while Pupitar uses Helping Hand or its own attack
strategy_checks.result: FAIL on turn 1, PASS on turn 3
strategy_checks.evidence: T1: Wyatt switched Gabite out and Pupitar used Helping Hand in the same turn - 'The opposing Pupitar used Helping Hand! But it failed!' Pupitar's entire turn was spent on a move that could not work. T3 the same pair of decisions was made correctly: Helping Hand resolved and Pupitar was 'ready to help', though Shelgon was KO'd before it could spend the boost. So the intent is implemented and it fired once out of two attempts, with the failure caused by a switch decided in the same turn. See ai_defects.

strategy_checks.check: Shelgon's Dragon Dance and Turtonator's Shell Smash fire, without exposing successive setup users
strategy_checks.evidence: Turtonator arrived on T1 with 98 HP, was taken to 6 by a single Ice Fang and died to Ice Shard on T2 without acting on a setup turn; it chose Heat Wave, not Shell Smash, on the one action it selected. Shelgon arrived on T2 and used Brick Break, not Dragon Dance, then died to Triple Axel. In both cases attacking was correct on the board they were given, so this is not a scoring failure - it is that neither setup route survives contact with a team that answers the whole roster with Ice.

strategy_checks.check: Turtonator's White Herb is consumed by Shell Smash
strategy_checks.result: FAIL, and I removed it deliberately
strategy_checks.evidence: My Weavile's Knock Off, retargeted onto Turtonator when Gabite switched out, stripped the White Herb on the turn Turtonator arrived - 'Weavile knocked off the opposing Turtonator's White Herb'. That is the dossier's own crack, 'removing Eviolite/White Herb', executing on the first turn of the battle. The item was never used. Second block team in a row where the White Herb / Shell Smash line never fires (see Travis's Crustle at play_order 89).

strategy_checks.check: The three Eviolite pre-evolutions' bulk is real
strategy_checks.result: PASS on paper, irrelevant in play
strategy_checks.evidence: Pupitar at level 39 with 140 HP and an Eviolite is genuinely bulky and it still died to one Waterfall, because Water is 4x into Rock/Ground. Gabite at 111 with an Eviolite died to an Ice Shard - a 40 BP priority move - because Ice is 4x into Dragon/Ground. Shelgon, the only one without a 4x weakness to something I carried, needed a full three-hit Triple Axel. The Eviolite is doing its job; the typing is not.

strategy_checks.check: Pupitar supplies the Ground offense Gabite lacks
strategy_checks.evidence: Pupitar's three turns were Helping Hand (failed), Protect, and Helping Hand (landed). It never used Stomping Tantrum or Rock Slide. Given that it was partnered with a switching Gabite and then a dying Shelgon, the support choices were reasonable, but the team's only Ground attack never appeared.

T1 Wyatt withdrew Gabite for Turtonator. That is a correct read - I had just led with two Ice carriers into a Dragon/Ground that is 4x weak to Ice - and it is the only opponent trainer switch I saw anywhere in my twelve battles. It cost him the Helping Hand turn, but the switch itself was right.

protect_ledger.payoff: EXCELLENT. Blocked Mega Gyarados's Waterfall, which is 4x into Rock/Ground and, as turn 3 proved, was a guaranteed one-hit KO on its 140 HP body even through the Eviolite. A guard that denies an outright KO is the best possible payoff, and it was not repeated the following turn.

protect_ledger_note: One opposing Protect in four turns, out of three members that carry it, denying a certain KO, with no repetition. Turtonator also carries Protect and chose Heat Wave instead on its only action, which was wrong in hindsight but not unreasonable at 98 HP before it knew what Ice Fang would do.

ai_defects.defect: Helping Hand selected onto a partner the same team was switching out in the same turn
ai_defects.board: Opponent Gabite (battler 1, 111/111, Eviolite) and Pupitar (battler 3, 140/140, Eviolite) against my Weavile and Gyarados. Pupitar's authored role in the plan is 'Helping Hand or its own attack'.
ai_defects.chosen: Wyatt switched Gabite out for Turtonator, and Pupitar used Helping Hand. The engine reported 'But it failed!' and Pupitar's turn produced nothing.
ai_defects.better_action: Either keep Gabite in and Helping Hand it, or - given the switch was correct - have Pupitar use Stomping Tantrum or Rock Slide, or Protect. Any of the three is worth more than a guaranteed-failed support move. The switch and the Helping Hand were decided from the same turn-start state by the same side, so the conflict was visible without any knowledge of my commands.
ai_defects.note: This is the third instance in my block of the same underlying shape: two battlers on the same side scoring their actions in isolation and producing a combination that is worse than either action alone. The others are Shayla's Tsareena crashing High Jump Kick into a target its own partner's Surf was killing (play_order 92) and Shayla's simultaneous double Protect on turn 1. Worth tracing as one family in the pair scorer rather than three separate bugs. Helping Hand specifically should be checked against every authored Helping Hand owner in the campaign, since a switch is not the only way for the partner's action to invalidate it.

ai_notes: The turn-1 switch is genuinely good play and I want to credit it separately from the Helping Hand failure it collided with. Leading two Ice carriers into a 4x-weak Gabite is the most obvious threat on the board and the AI moved its Pokemon out of it. This is the only opponent switch I saw in twelve battles.

Every other individual decision was sound: Protect on the turn a 4x Waterfall was incoming, Brick Break rather than a Dragon Dance it would not live to use, Heat Wave rather than a Shell Smash at 98 HP.
The fight is nonetheless a 4-0 in four turns against the highest-levelled team in my block, which says the level offsets are not the axis that matters here.

level_changes.reason: Brief rule 5: first-attempt win with zero player faints. Turtonator is the clear lowest member at offset 1 against 4/5/4. I am deliberately applying only one of the two permitted bumps. Pupitar is already cap+3 and Gabite and Shelgon cap+2, and a team that loses 4-0 in four turns while three of its members sit above the player cap does not have a level problem - it has a typing problem. Raising the rest further would make the encounter slower without making it harder for anyone who brings an Ice move, and more punishing for anyone who does not.

rerun_status: NOT RERUN. Opponent levels are compiled into the headless ROM from src/data/trainers.party and this agent may not run make. Pending the main agent's materialization and rebuild.
could_this_be_cooler: The concept - a collector who fields armoured adolescents rather than evolving them, with Eviolites and levels above the cap standing in for evolution - is one of the better ideas in the block and the dossier defends it well. The execution has one flaw that the high levels actively hide: Gabite is 4x weak to Ice, Pupitar is 4x weak to Water and Grass, and Shelgon is 2x weak to Ice, so a single Ice attacker and a single Water attacker cover the entire team, and both are trivially available at this point in the game. Turtonator, the one member that breaks the pattern, is also the lowest level and the first to die. I would raise Turtonator's role rather than its level: move it to the lead alongside Pupitar so the Shell Smash and the White Herb get a turn to exist before the Ice attacker has picked off the pre-evolutions, and consider a Yache Berry on Gabite the way Lawrence's Torterra carries one. That preserves every species, the Eviolite theme and the above-cap levels, and it would have made this fight considerably harder than four levels would.
